title: Kahana vs Etsy: Discovery Beside Checkout

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Digital trends (printables, templates, planners, niche ebooks) power many four- and five-figure monthly Etsy shops.
Fee structure (2026): listing USD 0.20 per item; transaction ~6.5% of item price + shipping; payment processing ~3% + USD 0.25; optional offsite ads ~12–15% of attributed orders.

strengths.title: Built-in traffic and search
strengths.detail: Marketplace search, category browsing, and Etsy ads can bring buyers without creators needing a separate audience.

strengths.title: Niche fit for creative digital products
strengths.detail: Strong for planners, templates, printables, guided journals, and design-forward ebooks, buyers expect creative goods.

strengths.title: Hybrid digital + physical
strengths.detail: Supports sellers offering both digital downloads and physical goods (prints, merch).

strengths.title: Seller tools and protections
strengths.detail: Shop analytics, listing tools, shipping labels, and buyer-protection frameworks.

weaknesses.title: Layered fees can be high
weaknesses.detail: Listing + transaction + processing + ads can substantially cut margins, especially at lower price points.

weaknesses.title: Marketplace competition and algorithm dependency
weaknesses.detail: Thousands of competing listings; visibility depends on Etsy’s algorithm and policy changes.

weaknesses.title: Limited branding and site control
weaknesses.detail: Stores live inside Etsy, limited layout customization; no custom domains or white-label.

weaknesses.title: Not digital-first
weaknesses.detail: Platform is geared toward physical crafts; pure text ebooks often need extra design and positioning to succeed.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Etsy is selling digital (or physical) goods through a store or marketplace. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Etsy is a global marketplace where people sell and buy unique goods, handmade items, vintage, craft supplies, and digital products (printables, templates, planners, niche ebooks).

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Etsy side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Etsy you can use Memberships and Marketplaces as first-class product jobs. The SKU is the product: a file, a theme, a craft listing, or a store you already operate.

Using Kahana with Etsy

You can use both. Etsy keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep Etsy for SKUs you already sell well. Put the curated collection on Kahana: a public hub on Explore, Aura as signal, and Stripe when you want a second place people can find and pay.
